headline: Las Vegas Sands reported $20.58M in Texas lobby "media" spending, 2021-26: 2.5 times all other lobbyists combined
number: $20,575,810.66 over 62 monthly reports by one lobbyist, Andy Abboud, May 2021-Jun 2026: 70-71% of all Texas lobby media (everyone else $8.26M), about 4x Sands' ~$5.1M federal lobby fees in the same months
watch_out: Abboud is a Sands employee (general knowledge, unchecked), so this may be Sands' own ad campaign filed under his name; don't write "a lobbyist spent."

headline: Reliant Care's 30 Missouri nursing homes log 35% fewer nurse hours and 3.8x the harm citations per bed
number: 2.16 vs 3.35 nurse hours per resident per day against other Missouri for-profit homes; 4.67 vs 1.23 harm citations per 100 beds (3.8x); fines $117,358 vs $27,138 per 100 beds (4.3x)
watch_out: Those 4 worst-list homes hold 76 of 141 harm citations; without them harm and fines are 2.5x, not 3.8x/4.3x. And it's 30 homes, not 31.

headline: Grain Processing's Iowa corn mill failed smokestack tests 49 days in 2015-25, no state order; Indiana twin: 7 orders
number: Muscatine IA 49 failed-test days (#1 of 29 big US wet corn mills), 36 violations, 0 orders; Washington IN 20 days, 7 Indiana orders, $687,030. Statewide 2015-25: Iowa 19 state air orders, Indiana 572
watch_out: The gap mirrors the two states, not this plant: Iowa barely files air orders at all. Split the Indiana mills' own 22 orders ($898,842) from EPA's 3 ($1.8M).

headline: In 2024, 20 clinicians billed Medicare $1.13B for skin-substitute wound patches; the makers reported paying them only $76,937
number: $1,126,228,007 billed by the top 20 in 2024 vs $76,937 in maker payments 2022-24 ($63,088 of it Organogenesis to Ravi Kapadia); 6 Arizona nurse practitioners billed only Impax, $124.0M (68.6% of all Impax)
watch_out: Denny (#20) and Palacios (#32, not top 20) tie to those Phoenix cases by surname and filing date only, and the charge is general fraud conspiracy, not health fraud.

headline: 19 police, fire, veteran and cancer-named political groups spent about $194M, mostly on fundraisers; $0.36M went to contributions
number: $193.7M by the groups' own IRS totals, 2014 to mid-2026 (itemized rows say $198.6M); 58% labelled fundraising or caging, 74% with telemarketing and mail; their donors are 15-74% of 13 look-alike FEC PACs' donor lists vs 6-9% for peer PACs
watch_out: The PACs' "7% to politics" is partly outside-spending paid to lead-list, caging and payment-processing vendors, so it overstates real support for candidates.

headline: Two mail-order suppliers took $593.6M of the $649.2M Medicare paid for one kind of wound dressing (alginate) in 2024
number: $593,632,181 of $649,233,082 (91.4%); one claim per patient a year, carrying 494 dressings (Sunshine Senior Solutions) and 359 (Almaz Med Supply) vs 55 per claim elsewhere; 5-11x peers per patient
watch_out: Almaz is on no ban list, and its absence from Medicare's enrollment file (PECOS) is normal for new big billers, so it proves nothing; drop "1.35 a day."

headline: 11% of San Antonio hospice ID numbers sit in "farms": one signer, 4+ hospice names, one address. Elsewhere: 0.5%
number: 31 of 282 active San Antonio hospice IDs (11.0%) vs 0.53% outside California, Houston and San Antonio; Houston 4-7%, California 3.3%; Houston's Suite 610 five trace to two signers, in a building holding 14 hospice IDs since 2008
watch_out: No hospice payment data exists in the warehouse, so nothing shows any of these IDs billed Medicare a dollar; and the signer isn't necessarily the owner.

headline: Counties flooded with opioid pills in 2006-12 had 2x the overdose death rate in 2019-24, and were already dying faster
number: 40.8 vs 20.2 overdose deaths per 100k, 2019-24, across 1,832 counties of 20K+ people (2.0x; holds at 1.9-2.1x); Knox County TN #27 of 1,832 at 74.5; Food City #674 took 31% of Knox's 30mg+ oxycodone
watch_out: Drop the AmerisourceBergen hook: it was the chain's normal wholesaler, and every distributor shipped these stores a strong mix. Split 30mg immediate-release from extended-release.

headline: Phoenix's weather office logged 63% of the heat deaths in the federal storm file, then stopped filing heat after June 2024
number: 1,345 of 2,145 US direct heat deaths in 2018-23 came from the Phoenix office; national direct heat deaths went 557 (2023), 250 (2024), 99 (2025), and without Phoenix they still halved, 205 to 98.
watch_out: The drop is paperwork, not fewer deaths: Phoenix copied Maricopa County's counts from 2018 on and then stopped, and Tucson and Las Vegas moved deaths from direct to indirect in 2025.

headline: SpaceX sites ran 3.2x their industry's injury rate in 2025, a third straight year; Ford about 1.9x big automakers
number: SpaceX's own sites 3.2x their industry (3.6x in 2024); Bath Iron Works 2.7x (3.0x); Ford 11.4 cases per 100 workers vs GM 6.5, Honda 6.8, Tesla 5.9, Toyota 5.2, about 1.9x.
watch_out: Name tags catch contractors (SpaceX janitors and valet crews), "Ingalls" was really Newport News, and this updates F-035 to F-037 rather than finding something new.

headline: One urgent-care chain, Fast Pace, holds 189 of 731 new for-profit rural health clinics opened after the 2021 pay law
number: 189 of the 731 new for-profit freestanding rural health clinics (26%), all enrolled from 2021-11-23 on; 192 counting 3 Louisiana clinics under the Fast Pace trade name.
watch_out: The enrollment date is read from inside ENROLLMENT_ID, and about 1 in 8 new enrollments reuse an older CCN, so some may be owner changes, not new clinics.

headline: Share of ICE jail-hold requests (detainers) on people with a criminal conviction fell from 43% to 16%, FY23 to FY26
number: 43% (October-March FY23) to 16% (October-March FY26), same months both years; FY25 was 33% on matching months.
watch_out: The drop lands exactly where one yearly file ends and the next begins, and the FY26 file was cut on 2026-03-11.

headline: Federal car-safety regulators' Nissan Rogue phantom-braking probe has sat open 7 years, no recall; the typical probe takes 234 days
number: Probe PE19010, opened 2019-09-09, open 2,572 days with no recall; the median defect probe closes in 234 days.
watch_out: Complaint counts swing with the matching method (component code: 75 before, 273 after; complaint text: 135 before, 224 after), and by text the yearly rate fell after the probe opened.

headline: New Mexico police cleared 22-23% of homicides in 2022-23, lowest in the nation, against 56% nationally
number: 22.3% (2022) and 23.2% (2023) by the FBI's state totals, lowest of 51 both years, vs 56% nationally; the fall was one year, 2018, from 59% to 34%.
watch_out: State totals can't tell police solving fewer killings from solved cases never reaching the FBI, and a one-year cliff looks like a reporting change.

headline: People arrested 2+ years after arriving had ICE bond posted 7% of the time in Louisiana, 29% in Pennsylvania
number: 7% in Louisiana, 12% in Texas, 29% in Pennsylvania, 2023-25, for people arrested 2+ years after entry.
watch_out: The bond field fills when bond is posted, not when a judge sets it, and border states hold recent arrivals who can't get bond at all.

headline: Nebraska air regulators filed zero formal enforcement actions 2017-2025; none of 17 serious violations from 2017-21 is resolved
number: 0 state and local formal air actions every year 2017-2025 in EPA's air database; 0 of 17 high-priority violations found 2017-21 marked resolved, vs 94% at the median state; 15 of 120 operating majors currently "Unaddressed" (12.5% vs a 1.4% median).
watch_out: "State" includes the Lincoln and Omaha local offices, and NDEE may settle by consent orders that never get typed into EPA's system.

headline: Three people on the federal health-fraud ban list are listed owners of six LA home health agencies
number: Liana Karapetyan (barred 2023, owns Direct Care HH), Kristine Arutyunyan (barred 2024, owns Holy Light and May Light HH), Arman Danielian (barred 2026-01-20, still listed at Vita, Valeo and Arva HH).
watch_out: These are name matches; the "2.6x more than chance" headline broke once surname geography was counted, and only these three, whose ban record is in the same line of work, survive.

headline: Judge Gilstrap was assigned 183 cases naming Apple, Microsoft, AT&T or Walmart while holding their stock
number: 183 cases assigned while he held the company's stock (disclosure years 2010-20); the wider 240-judge, 1,157-case total is not re-checked.
watch_out: It rests on Gilstrap alone, and holdings are matched by company-name text, not by a stock ID.

headline: 553 water permits broke pollution limits in 36+ of 40 quarters; 84 never had a formal enforcement action
number: 553 permits in 36+ of 40 quarters, 2016-2025; 152 with no formal action since 2016 and 84 with none ever, in EPA's system; in West Virginia, chronic mines got formal action 26% of the time vs 58% for chronic sewer plants.
watch_out: Every count is an absence in EPA's system, and West Virginia's mine enforcement barely flows into it, so "no action" may just mean "not reported."

headline: US rail trespasser deaths rose 26% to 838 from 2017 to 2025 while other rail casualties fell
number: 838 trespasser deaths in 2025, up 26% from 2017; all 41 Brightline deaths in 2024 were trespassers.
watch_out: The ledger calls it a known story shape, so check prior coverage before pitching it as new.

headline: $79,647 of lobbyist-paid private air and hotel: a New York trip with Sen. Angela Paxton and three Texas House members
number: $79,647.58 on one corrected March 2026 report by lobbyist Julie Linn Minnehan: private air to New York March 30-31 and one night at the Hilton Midtown; 3rd-biggest of 3,448 reports since 1992 (median $188); clients listed as Success Academy and Kleinheinz Capital Partners.
watch_out: Seven people flew up and Rep. Jeff Leach rode only the home leg; the data can't show who owned the plane or whether it was one plane.

headline: 40 big California water systems serving 4.2M people have no full sanitary inspection on EPA's file in 5 years
number: 40 California systems, 4.22M people, mostly in LA, San Bernardino, Riverside and San Diego counties; 35 of the original 41 show no visit of any kind since mid-2021. Nationally 94 systems, 7.66M people, counted from each state's real data end.
watch_out: All of this is absence in EPA's federal copy; New Jersey's gaps look like visits logged under another code, not missed surveys.

headline: Dow's Plaquemine, Louisiana plant reported 34,369 lb of ethylene oxide air release in 2023, 21% of the US total
number: 34,369 lb in 2023 (32,106 lb of it leaks), 8.7x its 2015-22 high and 21% of the 2023 national total (160,219 lb); back to 2,433 lb in 2024.
watch_out: No skeptic has checked it, and a one-year spike is most likely a single upset event already reported to the state.

headline: Of auditor Ben Borgers' 218 public-company clients, 27 moved to four Nigerian firms and 75 show no later audit
number: Of 218 clients audited in 2023-24, 143 found a new auditor (54 at one-partner firms, 72 at 2-5 partner firms, 17 at bigger firms), 27 of them at four Nigerian firms; 75 show no later audit.
watch_out: Borgers himself is the SEC's famous 2024 case; a second skeptic (skeptic2 g4) kept "135 of 218 filed no new audit," which misses the CIK matches.

headline: Where EPA found hazardous-waste violations, Illinois state inspectors of the same site wrote one up 15.5% of the time
number: Same site within 2 years, 2015-25: Illinois 15.5% (41 EPA inspections), New Jersey 28.5%, Pennsylvania 34.5%, nation 49.1% (1,202), Wisconsin 80.8%.
watch_out: This counts what states log, not what they miss, and Illinois and New Jersey rates about doubled after 2020, so the gap is shrinking.

headline: Sen. Markwayne Mullin filed 48 stock trades from 2023-24 in summer 2025; 46 were over a year late
number: 48 trade lines, 46 more than a year late, 244-953 days, at least $1.74M; Alan Armstrong's 701 late lines are one advisor-run account filed about 4 months late.
watch_out: Late filing is a steady trickle (11-59 late lines a year without Armstrong), so this is a named case, not a trend.

headline: Doctors paid $10K+ by drug companies wrote prescriptions costing 1.2-5.6x more per claim, more brand-name in all 7 specialties
number: In 2024, brand-name share rises with drug-company money in all 7 specialties, and $10K+ doctors cost 1.2-5.6x more per claim (internal medicine $94 to $355).
watch_out: Correlation only, and suppressed counts drop about 606K of 1.42M prescribers, so the sample leans to big prescribers.

headline: The UK sanctions 358 Russia shadow-fleet ships the US doesn't; 309 were listed in 2024-25
number: 358 of the 620 ships the UK sanctions under its Russia rules (58%) are not on OFAC's list (the US Treasury sanctions list); 309 of them were designated in 2024-25.
watch_out: No skeptic has checked it; trade press has covered this gap, and US Russia designations slowed in 2025 by policy.

headline: 634 poor-condition dams whose failure could kill people have no emergency plan, about 300 more than expected
number: 634 of 2,776 high-hazard dams rated Poor or Unsatisfactory answer a flat "No" (119 more say "Not Required"); against each state's good dams, the excess is about 300 (NC +45, NM +33, GA +32, SC +30, TX +29, MO +19).
watch_out: The warehouse's plan flag merges "No" and "Not Required," and Kentucky's big number is a state-wide "Not Required" code, not missing plans.

headline: Bankruptcy lawyers' groups paid for 41% of bankruptcy judges' trips in 2011-19, against 0.7% for other federal judges
number: 2,525 of 6,166 bankruptcy-judge trips (41.0%) paid by bankruptcy practitioner groups vs 0.7% for district and appeals judges; Delaware's Kevin Carey reported 200 trips, 25 paid by the Turnaround Management Association.
watch_out: No skeptic has checked it; speaking and teaching trips for these groups are permitted and routine, and the disclosures carry no dollar amounts.

headline: Illinois flags 30% of its nursing homes for abuse, three times the 9% rate everywhere else
number: 30% of Illinois homes carry the abuse flag vs 9% elsewhere; the Bria, Evercare and Infinity chains sit near 73%.
watch_out: The state explains most of it, and Bria alone is not unusual inside Illinois.

headline: San Antonio nurse practitioner Kim Hinojosa prescribed $24.9M of specialty drugs to Medicare patients in 2022, most of any NP
number: $24.9M of specialty Part D drugs in 2022 (hepatitis C, bowel disease and psoriasis drugs), then $1.37M in 2024; specialty peers run $12-19M.
watch_out: The community-clinic (FQHC) tie is a current-address join, not proof she worked there in 2022.

headline: Only 1 of 67,777 federal-grant auditees had survival doubts and rule-breaking flagged 10 years straight: Lower Brule Sioux Tribe
number: Going-concern doubt and material noncompliance in all 10 audit years, 2016-2025 (EIN 460222351); no other auditee has even 7 years of both. Federal spending $16.7M to $35.7M, $246.2M in all.
watch_out: The money doubling is normal for tribes (median 1.77x, mostly 2021 COVID money), so the story is the flag streak, not the dollars.

headline: 25 senior and disabled housing nonprofits on HUD money kept filing federal audits years after the IRS revoked their exemption
number: 25 groups, about $83M counting each group's biggest single year (not the $940M first claimed); 5 name-match active HUD Section 202 rent contracts in the same town.
watch_out: The dollars are mostly an old HUD capital advance carried on the books every year, not new spending, and the HUD match is on property name and place only.

headline: 54 high-overdose, high-jail counties got $45 per person of federal addiction-agency money in 2019-25, half their peers' $92
number: $45 per person of SAMHSA (federal substance-abuse agency) money, FY2019-25, in the 54 flagged counties vs $92 in same-size counties with the same overdose ranking; 22% of flagged counties got any vs 34%.
watch_out: No skeptic has checked it; most of this money is block grants booked where the state agency sits, and the median county in every group got $0.

headline: Nursing-home dialysis brands run 18 of 26 rated clinics flagged worse on survival, but only 9% worse than peers
number: Dialyze Direct, Dialysis Direct and Concerto: 31 clinics, 18 of 26 rated flagged Worse on survival; their nursing-home residents die at 1.61x expected vs 1.48x at other nursing-home-heavy units, about 9% worse.
watch_out: CMS's model under-predicts nursing-home deaths everywhere (1.18x expected), so these units start about 25% "worse" by construction; it's a class effect more than a brand effect.

headline: California family therapists opted out of Medicare at 37%, 3.5 times the rate of California social workers
number: CA marriage and family therapists 37.3% opt-out (decisions since 2024) vs social workers 10.7%; psychologists 31.6%; CA holds 70% of US family-therapist opt-outs.
watch_out: Psychologists run close to family therapists (1.2x), California runs high for every profession, and opting out can just mean a big cash-pay senior market.

headline: 27% of 919 nonprofit hospitals paid one officer more than their whole 2022 charity-care cost
number: 27% of 919 nonprofit hospitals had one officer's 2022 pay above the hospital's entire cost of charity care.
watch_out: The ledger says "confirmed with caveats" without listing them, and only crosswalk match tiers 1-2 are used, so hospitals outside the crosswalk are missing.

headline: 193 providers on the federal health-fraud ban list took about $166K from drug companies in 2024
number: 193 banned NPIs paid about $166K in 2024; one row is $114K (Hector Molina, TX, "debt forgiveness" from Skye Orthobiologics).
watch_out: One row carries most of the dollars, and WAS_REINSTATED is False on every row, so that filter removes nothing.

headline: loanDepot denied 74% of refinance applications in 2015-17 but only 8% of home-purchase ones
number: 74% of refinance applications denied vs 8% of purchase applications, below Wells Fargo's 15%; the first pass said 56% on all rows.
watch_out: The story flipped once loan purpose was split: loanDepot is a low-denial purchase lender, so always split by purpose before ranking lenders.

headline: All 11 Justice Department Epstein data-set pages lost their 'Download all files' link between Jan 30 and Feb 9, 2026
number: 11 of 11 data-set pages lost the .zip link between Jan 30 and Feb 9, 2026, and none got it back through early June; 12 court-case links were renamed to "[redacted] v. ..." on Feb 21 and 24.
watch_out: No skeptic has checked it; both changes fit a victim-privacy cleanup after the Jan 30 release, and the plaintiff names are already in public court records.

headline: Eight coal-mine owners logged 900-1,960 serious safety violations per 1,000 miners in 2018-24
number: 900-1,960 significant-and-substantial violations per 1,000 current miners, 2018-24, for eight mine controllers.
watch_out: No skeptic has checked it; the denominator is today's headcount, not 2018-24 staffing, and it's per miner, not per inspection day.

headline: Roosevelt Cayman Asset Company filed a third of Puerto Rico's federal foreclosures in 2015-25; 52% ended in default judgment
number: About 1,130 separate foreclosure cases; 52% of first filings ended in default vs 37% for other Puerto Rico filers; about 11 points once years are matched, all of it from 2015-16.
watch_out: The whole gap comes from the 2015-16 wave (in 2017-18 Roosevelt was level with or below peers), and a second skeptic (skeptic2) put the year-matched gap at only about 6 points.

headline: Changes to high-risk medical devices filed as 30-day notices, skipping full FDA review, rose from 19% to 64%
number: 19% of approval changes in 2000-04 to 64% from 2010 on; one Medtronic defibrillator line (P980016) has 928 changes, 621 of them 30-day notices.
watch_out: No skeptic has checked it; long-lived pacemaker and defibrillator lines pile up manufacturing changes, and the device-problem reports here cover only 2020-01 to 2021-09.

headline: Rural jails now lock up 2.5 times the urban rate: 563 vs 227 per 100,000 working-age residents in 2023
number: In 1,906 fixed counties, rural jails went 531 to 624 per 100K residents aged 15-64 (2010-19), then 563 in 2023, while urban fell 335 to 227; Butts GA and Yazoo MS grew about 4x on local holds.
watch_out: No skeptic has checked it; Vera published the rural jail boom itself, and the held-for-others columns go blank after 2020.

headline: One pension plan (EIN 822871833) is 25.8% funded with $95.4M unpaid; Transit Management of Southeast Louisiana shows $79.5M unpaid
number: 631 single-employer plans report $426.7M in unpaid minimum contributions for 2024; EIN 822871833 is 25.8% funded with $95.4M unpaid; Transit Management of Southeast Louisiana shows $79.5M unpaid.
watch_out: No skeptic has checked it; for 201 plans the "unpaid" amount equals exactly this year's minimum, which points to filing before the payment deadline, not arrears.

headline: 92 political committees each raised $1M+ from individuals in 2024 ($580M total) but passed under 10% to candidates or ads
number: 92 non-joint-fundraising PACs, $580M from individuals, each sending under 10% of spending to candidates, committees, outside ads or affiliates; the 12 busiest treasurers have 29 of 96 such PACs (30%) vs 14.6% for everyone else.
watch_out: No skeptic has checked it; canvassing, digital ads not reported as outside spending, conduits and legal bills all look like a "low share."

headline: About 89 active Texas major air polluters have had no full compliance inspection in 5+ years; New Mexico is worse
number: About 89 of 2,481 Texas majors (3.6 per 100) with activity on their own permit since mid-2021 but no full evaluation in 5+ years, vs a 0.2 state median; New Mexico 23 of 160 (14.4 per 100).
watch_out: All four plants first named had a twin record at the same site that did get evaluated; a second skeptic (skeptic2) got Texas at 3.0 per 100 and New Mexico at 12.5.

headline: Aircraft Guaranty Corp's trustee arm holds 364 live US plane registrations and added 38 in 2024-26, after 1 in 2021-23
number: 364 valid, unexpired tail numbers at one Oklahoma City address; new certificates 2024: 6, 2025: 18, 2026: 14, against 1 in 2021 and 1 in 2023.
watch_out: No skeptic has checked it; the conviction tie comes from press reports, not verified, and trustee registration is legal and common.

headline: Serious water-system defects found before 2022 are still unfixed in 19% of West Virginia cases, against 3% elsewhere
number: Pre-2022 unfixed inspection-defect cases still open: West Virginia 19.0%, EPA-run tribal land in Region 9 11.3%, Louisiana 8.8%, other states 3.0%; open 2+ years: WV 218, LA 337, Region 9 48.
watch_out: The physical thing is an unfixed inspection defect, not contaminated water, and Region 9 logs close-outs a median 478 days late.

headline: For-profit nursing homes: 3.70 staff hours per resident a day vs 4.40 at nonprofits; fines $320 vs $205 a bed
number: 10,851 for-profit homes at 3.70 staff hours per resident per day vs 2,908 nonprofits at 4.40; fines $320 vs $205 per bed; Arcadia Care is the worst chain at $1,357 per bed.
watch_out: No skeptic has checked it; the penalty file is CMS's rolling 3-year window, not lifetime fines, and the story itself is well known.

headline: Five firms at one Newington, Connecticut, address won $13.35M in 41 small-business research awards; the Air Force barred all five
number: $13.35M in 41 SBIR awards, 2021-25, to five firms at 549 Cedar St, Newington CT; the Air Force barred all five on 2026-07-17.
watch_out: The ban says "proceedings pending," not a finding of fault, and it is already public.

headline: Barred landlord Amerihost Services drew $1.54M in federal Section 8 rent subsidy in 27 payments during its 2021-26 ban
number: $1.54M in 27 HUD Section 8 payments, 2021-11 to 2026-03, inside an EPA ban running 2021-09-08 to 2026-09-07.
watch_out: It's one rent contract renewed every year since 2007, not new grants, and rent aid follows the tenants.

headline: US companies registered through Bloomberg refuse to name their ultimate owner 5.7% of the time; other registrars, 2.3%
number: Current US global company IDs (LEIs): 5.7% refuse to name the ultimate owner at Bloomberg vs 2.3% at every other registrar; 91% of US refusals sit at Bloomberg.
watch_out: Bloomberg's client mix (swap counterparties, fund vehicles) isn't ruled out, and the harm is unclear.

headline: Black home buyers were denied about twice as often as white buyers at every big 2017 mortgage lender
number: At every 2017 home-purchase lender with 500+ Black and 2,000+ white applications, the Black denial rate ran about 2x the white rate.
watch_out: No income or credit columns, so the gap can't be adjusted, and it's a known shape.

headline: NYC's 2025 mayor race: one committee, Fix the City, took $35.6M from 381 gifts; Mamdani raised $4.03M from 54,103
number: Fix the City $35.6M from 381 gifts; Mamdani $4.03M from 54,103 gifts, after 302 refund rows were removed.
watch_out: Confirmed, but it's a known story from the 2025 race.

headline: 706 finished US drug and device trials, 8.6% of those the law covers, never posted results: 152,850 patients
number: 706 of 8,234 FDA-regulated US phase 2-4 trials that finished 2017-01-18 to 2022-06-30 have no results as of 2026-09-04, covering 152,850 enrolled patients.
watch_out: A long tail: 435 of 537 sponsors miss exactly one, and TrialsTracker already ranks sponsors.

headline: Among diabetes shots, doctors paid only by Novo (Ozempic's maker) chose Ozempic 54% of the time; unpaid doctors 41%
number: Prescribers with 50+ Ozempic/Rybelsus plus Trulicity claims in 2022: paid only by Novo 54% Ozempic, paid by neither 41%.
watch_out: Correlation only: half the gap was there before the money arrived.

headline: Elgin, Illinois, tests at 53 parts per billion of lead; about 17 big water systems are over the limit now
number: About 17 systems serving 10K+ people are over the 15 ppb lead line on their newest test (19 before the skeptic); Elgin reads 53 ppb, over in 7 of 13 tests.
watch_out: The other Illinois towns jumped only after the state's 2025 testing change; Elgin was over before it.

headline: Nevro's spinal-cord stimulator has 168 death reports out of 737 (22.8%); similar devices run 0.18%
number: Nevro Senza: 168 death reports of 737 (22.8%); the rest of its product code: 76 of about 42,200 (0.18%); 0 of the 168 flag a device problem.
watch_out: Zero device-problem flags points at how Nevro reports, not harm; only 21 months (2020-01 to 2021-09) are loaded.

headline: 56,159 rural apartments in federal farm-agency housing opened by 1980 have no live low-rent clause; 35,324 get rent help
number: 56,159 units (13.5%) sit in projects opened by 1980 with no live restrictive clause; 35,324 get rental help; Iowa 36%, Missouri 32%.
watch_out: The clause dates follow a formula and the table has no loan due date; the outstanding loan can still bind the project.

headline: ACNR's underground coal mines logged 11.1 injuries per 100 workers a year, 2018-24; other big owners ran 2.2 to 8.8
number: ACNR 11.10 recordable injuries per 100 current workers a year, 2018-24; other big coal owners 2.24-8.81; Foresight 12.33.
watch_out: The denominator is today's headcount, and ACNR's lead is sprains booked as days away; on fractures it's mid-pack.

headline: 5,362 company officers and directors match $555M of federal campaign gifts by name, state and employer
number: 5,362 SEC insiders (officer or director filings 2021-25) matched to $555M of $1,000+ individual FEC gifts, 2022-26 cycles; coal CEO Joseph Craft III gave $8.2M.
watch_out: A name-and-employer match never skeptic-checked; the bridge is worth more than the story.

headline: Sea Robin pipeline's 2025 gas-loss reports reuse one number, 1,587,069, whole, halved and split three ways
number: 1,587,069 filed whole (May 17), as two 793,534 halves (Jan 13) and, minus 3,508, as three 527,853 blowdowns; counted once, 2025 is still the record at about 3.5M vs 2.98M in 2022.
watch_out: No unit column: if Sea Robin typed cubic feet instead of thousand cubic feet, 2025 falls to about 1.94M, an ordinary year.

headline: Acetaminophen-codeine liquid's generic price jumped 30-fold in 2024; saxagliptin tablets rose 4.2x, then 4.9x
number: Of 308,054 same-unit generic price steps in 2024, 20 were 3x+ up; acetaminophen-codeine solution $0.0145 to $0.434 per mL; saxagliptin 5 mg $1.35 to $6.67.
watch_out: Only 2024's weekly files are loaded, and shortages and makers leaving explain most jumps.

headline: Diamondback hides 30.3% of its Texas fracking chemicals as trade secrets, nearly double the 16.2% state rate
number: Diamondback withholds 30.3% of its Texas chemical-ID rows vs 16.2% statewide, with secrets in 96.7% of its 3,164 jobs.
watch_out: No job dates on any row, and trade-secret claims are legal and industry-wide.

headline: DeKalb County's Snapfinger Creek sewer plant logged 1,394 overflows since 2016 against $52,344 in penalties: about $38 each
number: Snapfinger Creek (GA0024147): 1,394 overflows since Oct 2016, 4 formal actions, $52,344 in penalties since 2015; 202 overflows in 2025, its high.
watch_out: A known consent-decree story, and overflow counts map which states report (only 21-36 do).

headline: 94 ex-members of Congress later filed foreign-agent forms; five filed in 2025, including Blagojevich for Bosnia and Fattah for Liberia
number: 94 ex-members (left office 1970 or later) filed FARA short forms after leaving; 26 first filed 2017+; 5 in 2025: Wexler, Blagojevich, Stewart, Fattah, Seymour (weak match).
watch_out: Name-only match with at least one sure miss ("Stephanie Jones" filed in 2019; Stephanie Tubbs Jones died in 2008), and no dollars.

headline: 143 doctor-shortage areas first flagged in 1978-89 are still flagged; 31 still rank severe, mostly Mississippi Delta and South Texas
number: 143 of 999 still-designated primary-care areas date from 1978-89; 31 still score 18+ (Humphreys, Jefferson, Copiah MS 22; Jim Hogg TX 23).
watch_out: Designations double as funding applications, so they persist; chronic rural shortage is well known.

headline: Beaver Valley Hospital, 25 beds in Utah, took $22.3M in COVID relief: 2.45 times its 2019 patient revenue
number: $22.3M relief vs $9.1M 2019 net patient revenue (2.45x); 40 Utah nursing-home enrollments carry the hospital's name.
watch_out: The rural tranche paid critical-access hospitals more by design (median 19.8% of revenue).

headline: Political ad buyers who gave Google only a tax ID, no federal election ID, spent $861.4M on Google ads
number: 8,368 EIN-only US buyers spent $861.4M (FEC-ID buyers $1,389.1M); Securing American Greatness Inc put 84% of its 2024 spend on one-gender ads.
watch_out: State candidates and ballot committees have no federal election ID by law, so most of the pile is legal.

headline: CareCore Health's 12 Ohio nursing homes draw 1.95x their state's fire-safety citations; 11 repeat a citation across three inspections
number: CareCore (OH, 12 homes) 1.95x its state's fire citations per home; 11 of 12 repeat a tag in all 3 cycles (2.54x the state rate); median chain 1.00x.
watch_out: Almost all sprinkler and alarm-testing upkeep (K0353, K0345), with 0-1 serious citations per chain.

headline: One Egyptian national born in 2001 controls 630 UK companies the register calls live; none file accounts
number: 630 companies where he's a not-ceased controlling person, notified 2022-26, none filing accounts, most at one Manchester business centre.
watch_out: Not-ceased control is not a live company (Southern: 0 of 759 alive); likely a company-formation agent.

headline: 68 federal district judges with unusual loans from a bank were assigned 424 cases naming that bank
number: 379 judges got 3,650 cases naming a bank they owed that year (2003-21); the narrow cut is 68 district judges with investment, guaranty or $250K+ loans on 424 cases.
watch_out: Under recusal law an ordinary loan isn't ownership, so most hits are routine.

headline: The federal housing agency pays $2,574 a unit a month for White Birch Apartments in Milwaukee: 223% of fair rent
number: $2,574 a unit a month, 223% of fair rent for its bedroom mix; no other 100+ unit building in a cheap market outside Puerto Rico runs a higher ratio.
watch_out: Two tax-credit deals in seven years (2017 FHA purchase, May 2024 new owner) fit a legal rent reset.

headline: 29 Medicare-enrolled businesses are signed for by someone sharing a banned person's name, city and state; two drew $4.91M
number: 29 enrolled orgs, org NPI created after the ban; 2 drew 2024 Part B money: National Health Transport (Miami ambulance) $4.25M, ASAP EMS (Laurel MS) $662K.
watch_out: Raul Rodriguez and Kevin Smith are common names, so namesakes aren't ruled out.

headline: 33 US healthcare posts on ransomware leak sites match a Medicare hospital by name; Watsonville's was posted by two gangs
number: 1,146 US healthcare posts; 33 match a Medicare hospital (32 hospitals); Watsonville Community Hospital posted by termite (2024-12) and sinobi (2025-10).
watch_out: A leak-site post is not a confirmed breach.

headline: Altair Recycling in Texas got a $57.0M state water-pollution penalty in June 2025, the biggest on file after BP's
number: $57.0M state civil judicial penalty on 2025-06-06 (case TX-D-1-GN-19-002002), biggest after BP's two $3.35B lines; hazardous-waste violations open since 2019.
watch_out: One site; the water fine and the waste violations are tied by name, not by an ID.

headline: On a strict name and birth-date match, 22 sanctioned people control 46 live UK companies; about 3 are likely chance
number: Strict full-name match, open control, Active company: 22 people on 46 companies (loose count was 45 on 83); a shifted-birth-month test finds about 3 by chance.
watch_out: Kong isn't a find: OFAC's own 2026-06-23 action names 6 of his UK companies by number.

headline: Two cases went to judges whose spouses drew director fees from the defendant: McMahon–JetBlue, Leinenweber–Procter & Gamble
number: Liotti v. Jet Blue (SDNY 1:17-cv-00838, closed in 5 days; spouse's JetBlue fees 2014-18) and Gardner v. Procter & Gamble (NDIL 1:09-cv-06690; spouse's P&G fees 2004-09).
watch_out: CourtListener holds only dockets someone pulled, so hits are floors, and recusal isn't ruled out.

headline: Drug companies logged 47,607 doctor meals at exactly $125.00 in 2024, against 675 at $126.00
number: 2024 meals: 47,607 at $125.00 and 20,666 at $124.99 vs 675 at $126.00 and 192 at $123.99; AstraZeneca 11.1 per 1,000 meals just under $125, Pfizer 0.6.
watch_out: $125 is a company policy cap, not a law, so this is a fingerprint, not harm.

headline: E-bike and moped emergency-room visits quadrupled, 21,800 to 87,600 a year from 2019 to 2023, while all injuries stayed flat
number: E-bikes plus mopeds (code 3215, split into 5045 and 5046 in 2024): 21.8K to 87.6K weighted ER visits, 2019 to 2023 (4.0x); all injuries 0.95x.
watch_out: Weights reset in 2024 and floor injuries jumped in 2025, so don't read trends past 2023.

headline: Outside money beat the candidate's own spending in 104 of 637 congressional campaigns in 2024; Moreno tops at 5.8x
number: 104 of 637 matched 2024 House and Senate candidates saw more outside spending than their own (82 over $1M); Moreno $152M outside vs $26M own.
watch_out: 29 crank rows hold $115B and must be filtered; the famous Senate races top every list.

headline: Forest County, Pennsylvania, has 1,685 orphaned oil and gas wells for every 10,000 residents
number: Forest PA 1,685 per 10K people; Monroe OH 1,491; Nowata OK 1,441; Venango PA holds 4,786 wells, 25% of Pennsylvania's.
watch_out: One 2019-22 snapshot with no operator column, and counts track how hard each state looked.

headline: Delaware's court got 46 of the 80 billion-dollar business bankruptcies filed since 2015, counting affiliated cases as one
number: Delaware 46 of 80 Chapter 11 families with $1B+ assets (57.5%) vs 3.2% of all families; Houston has 58 families of 20+ affiliates, 52 showing under $1M assets.
watch_out: The dollar columns failed (Houston's assets are blank, "debt discharged" isn't), and venue shopping is well covered.

headline: 76 co-authors of papers retracted in federal misconduct cases got $187M in federal health-research grants afterward
number: 76 US co-authors of ORI-investigated retractions (2010-25) got $187M in NIH awards noticed after the retraction.
watch_out: Can't tell the person who faked data from the lab head; the closing skeptic reads it as C.

headline: 23 firms under a government-wide ban got $800K in new federal orders after the ban, mostly from Defense
number: 23 firms under Reciprocal or Procurement exclusions got about $800K of positive new actions after the ban, mostly DoD.
watch_out: A real join but small money.

headline: Hedge funds and banks paid for 14.6% of itemized Texas lobby meals; the top recipient got $10-14K over 15 years
number: Firm-named filers paid 2,114 of 14,448 itemized meals (14.6%, about 22% of range-high dollars); Brad Gilbert got 70 meals worth $10.2K-$14.4K from 11 funds, 2011-26.
watch_out: Itemized meals are only 3.5% of reported food money, so this ranks what got itemized.

headline: NAI Logistics got 13 Defense fuel payments worth a net $20,647 within 3 days of its sanctions listing
number: NAI Logistics B.V.: $3.28M over 436 DoD actions; 13 actions, net $20,647, dated on or up to 3 days after its 2023-12-11 Global Magnitsky listing.
watch_out: FIRST_SEEN is when OpenSanctions picked the entry up, not the designation date.

headline: Oklahoma lost 161 veterans to suicide in 2023, against 98 to 134 every year from 2011 to 2022
number: 161 in 2023 vs 98-134 a year in 2011-22; about z=3.3 for 2023 alone against the national trend, the top state but not unique (Indiana 2022, z=3.64).
watch_out: One bad year, not a trend; the "4.9 SD" and Kansas claims broke under the skeptic.

headline: Tesla has 43 California accident inspections by job-safety regulators; 18 are still open, with a median 486 days to close
number: Tesla: 44 accident or fatality inspections since 2015, 43 in California; 18 still open; median 486 days to close vs 139-251 for most top employers.
watch_out: California files serious-injury inspections as type A where other states use M, and there's no headcount.

headline: Redlined 1930s neighborhoods hold 13.35 toxic-release plants per 100 square kilometers, six times the 2.21 in 'B' areas
number: Toxic-release plants per 100 km²: D areas 13.35, C 5.82, B 2.21, A 0.07; D denser than B in 119 of 212 cities.
watch_out: The plants likely came before the maps, and redlining-to-pollution research is already published.

headline: Black residents' jail rate ran 4.57x the white rate in 2010, 3.41x in 2019 and 3.86x in 2023, median county
number: Median Black/white jail-rate ratio in 356 fixed counties: 4.57 (2010), 3.41 (2019), 3.86 (2023); counties at 10x+: 30, 19, 24.
watch_out: This table is Vera's data re-served (0 differences), and the post-2020 rise crosses a race-coding break.

headline: 987 of 22,770 months where an insider sold $5M+ of stock came 4-9 months before a 50%+ price drop
number: 987 of 22,770 owner-months with $5M+ sold (2015-25) preceded a price at least 50% lower; e.g. Daniel Loeb in Upstart, $712M at $225, later $51.
watch_out: The top of the list is stock splits (Tesla, Walmart, Alphabet), and preset trading plans can't be checked.

headline: Oklahoma refineries pay $3,300 in air penalties per logged violation; Texas refineries pay $142,000
number: Refinery-coded sites 2015-25: Oklahoma 9 sites, 148 violations, $0.48M penalties ($3.3K each); Texas 58 sites, 203 violations, $28.8M ($142K each).
watch_out: Only 9 facilities, and states differ in what they report into this federal file.

headline: CSX and Norfolk Southern made 8.2 times the spill-hotline calls of Union Pacific and BNSF in 2015-17
number: CSX plus Norfolk Southern 511 calls a year vs 63 for Union Pacific plus BNSF, 2015-17 (8.2x); 140 vs 76.5 in 2024-25 (1.8x).
watch_out: Self-reported call headers only, with no material, amount or place, and habits differ by railroad.

headline: In two environmental-agency regions, 78% of hazardous-waste sites inspected twice have no action on file, versus 33% in two others
number: RCRA sites inspected on-site twice or more since 2015: no EPA case or informal action on file at 78% in Regions 6 and 9 vs 33% in Regions 7 and 8.
watch_out: The case tables carry no dates, so "no action" means none ever, not none after the inspection.

headline: Kings County, California, rejected 13.7% of returned mail ballots in 2022, against 1.52% nationally
number: Kings County CA rejected 13.7% of returned mail ballots in 2022 (3,628 under unlabeled reason C9P) vs 1.52% nationally.
watch_out: Some counties book undeliverable mail as rejections (Orange, Los Angeles, Hernando); read the "other" labels first.

headline: 37 planes that crash investigators rated destroyed got their federal registration renewed or extended after the crash
number: Of 420 destroyed US planes still marked valid, 383 sit inside a term that began before the crash; 37 had terms start after it, all touched in 2023.
watch_out: The 37 could be rebuilds (mostly warbirds, helicopters, homebuilts) or FAA batch processing.

headline: Senators on the Banking Committee were 19% of trading senators but made 34% of bank-stock trades, 2012-20
number: Banking Committee members were 19% of trading senator-Congress pairs but made 34% of bank-stock trades, 2012-20.
watch_out: Perdue alone drives it; the closing skeptic reads it as C.

headline: 83 new Arizona hospices (2020-23) listed Los Angeles phone numbers; only 12 ever got Medicare certification, 4 still enrolled
number: 12 of 83 ever certified and 4 still on Medicare's enrollment roll, vs about 120 certified and 81 enrolled among the other 246 new Arizona hospices; 43 of the 83 registered in 2022 Q1, the quarter new LA-area hospice registrations fell to 3
watch_out: A hospice that enrolled and was later revoked drops off the current enrollment file, so "never enrolled" may really mean "revoked."

headline: Arizona overdose deaths rose 11.5% in a year as the median state fell 14%, hitting 2,980, its most since 2015
number: 2,980 deaths in the 12 months to Oct 2025 (old high 2,829, Aug 2023); cocaine-involved deaths 261 to 443 while the US figure fell 12%
watch_out: One dull explanation is untested: a change in how Maricopa's medical examiner certifies deaths.

headline: Generic makers Teva, Actavis and Mutual filed about 15,500 lawyer-sourced metoclopramide (Reglan) side-effect reports: 91% of the generic's reports
number: 9,089 arrived Apr-Sep 2011, when the FDA got about 16 a quarter in 2004-2009; the median drug has 0.05% lawyer-coded reports
watch_out: These are lawsuit claims sent in through the drugmaker, not a new safety signal, and the file ends 2014q2.

headline: Oroville Hospital, California, had 1.78 stays per traditional-Medicare patient, tied for highest of 2,109 big hospitals; median 1.34
number: 3,938 stays for 2,213 patients; sepsis codes on 30% of stays (1,194) vs a 15% California median
watch_out: The file has no data year and only one vintage, so nobody has tested whether 1.78 holds year to year.

headline: Medicare's ordering list still clears 83% of recently deactivated clinicians to order equipment; for older deactivations it's 0.2%
number: 1,036 of 1,247 2024 Part B billers deactivated Sep 2025-Jun 2026 are still on the list with the equipment flag Y (power wheelchairs Y on 71%); 2 of 1,040 for Oct 2024-Jun 2025; the sister list carries 10 of the 1,247
watch_out: One copy of the file can't tell a designed grace window from a hole, and no equipment claim paid after a deactivation is shown.

headline: 944 for-profit nursing homes with operating companies formed 2022 to Sept 2024 rate 0.28 stars below same-state for-profit peers
number: 52% are one- or two-star, 8 points above same-state for-profit homes; the median home sits 0.42 stars below
watch_out: The company formation date only stands in for a sale and goes blank after Sept 2024; "worse after the change" did not survive matching (+0.9 citations, t about 1.5).

headline: Five Los Angeles-area postal zones (ZIP 912-916) hold 35% of home health agencies enrolled since 2019; before 2013, 3%
number: 1,259 of 3,597 still-enrolled agencies that enrolled 2019 or later, vs 190 of 6,145 that enrolled before 2013; one Van Nuys building, 14545 Friar St, holds 49 agencies and 9 hospices
watch_out: The enrollment file lists only agencies still enrolled, so closed agencies are invisible (survivorship).

headline: Only 7 of 26 Indian Health Service and tribal hospitals have a Medicare star rating; similar hospitals predict about 13
number: 7 rated vs about 13 expected from same-state hospitals with as many Medicare stays; Fort Defiance, Tuba City and Chinle (Navajo area) are nearly half the gap
watch_out: A missing star can mean too few cases rather than a refusal to report; the footnotes that tell them apart aren't landed.

headline: Ingredient makers filed 83 semaglutide (Ozempic) files with the drug regulator since 2023, the biggest four-year rush since 1980
number: 83 files Jan 2023-Jun 2026 (65 for the ingredient itself, from 54 companies); next real wave tirzepatide 40, then esomeprazole 36; Harbin Jixianglong Biotech recalled semaglutide ingredient on 2026-02-13
watch_out: A master file is not an approval, and the 1990s antibiotic "waves" include a one-day paperwork batch (56 files dated 1998-09-01).

headline: The CDC's weekly disease table shows 17,197 cyclospora parasite infections by late July 2026, at least 5x any 2022-25 year
number: Michigan 7,395 and Ohio 4,408; six Midwest and Plains states hold 78%; best prior year at week 30 was 3,451 (2023, late reports included)
watch_out: Provisional data: Michigan's year-to-date is 5.3x the sum of its weekly counts, so about 6,000 cases arrived as back-filled totals.

headline: 24 of 72 Mississippi hospitals are worse than the national death rate on some measure; only 1 is better
number: Big hospitals in Mississippi, Arkansas, Alabama and Tennessee: 43 worse and 4 better, where look-alike hospitals predict about 20 and 25
watch_out: The table carries no release date, and CMS death models adjust for clinical risk, not income.

headline: Florida went from 17 freestanding rehab hospitals in mid-2019 to 40 now, +135%, with zero closures; rest of US +31%
number: 23 new hospitals and 1,144 beds, 0 closures; Florida's net +24 is the most of any state (Texas +26%)
watch_out: Hospital rehab-unit "openings" are mostly old units with reset dates, so only freestanding hospitals count.

headline: Rep. Thomas Kean (R-NJ) missed 140 recorded House votes in a row, 33 voting days, the longest run this Congress
number: 140 straight, 2026-03-17 to 2026-06-25, where the member-vote file ends; the median member's longest run is 3
watch_out: The member-vote file ends 2026-06-25, so the streak may be longer, and it is very likely already reported.

headline: 16 House members running for Senate doubled their missed votes in campaign season, but did the same two years earlier
number: Median missed rate 1.8% (Jan-Nov 2025) to 3.5% (Dec 2025-Jun 2026), other members flat; the same 16 rose 0.3% to 2.4% in the same months of 2023-24
watch_out: The placebo kills the cause: net of the same 16's rise two years earlier, the gap is not significant, and the menu says drop it.

headline: California employers naming artificial intelligence on lobbying reports: 1 in 2022, 58 in 2024, 59 in 2025
number: 1.8% of employers writing real activity text in 2024 and 2025, vs 0.03% in 2022; 45 in the first half of 2026
watch_out: Bill numbers repeat across sessions, so the 175-229 floor that counts AI bills by number holds only after that session check.

headline: Sean Duffy's old House fund raised $0 from donors but gave $1.5M to Northwoods Future PAC, about half its money
number: $1.5M in two checks (2025-10-27 and 2026-07-15); the $1M check is the biggest from any dormant campaign committee in 2025-26 (next: $215K); the PAC spent about $2.2M-$3.2M backing Michael Alfonso in Wisconsin's 7th
watch_out: Leftover campaign money can legally go to a super PAC; the story is the size and who it backs, not a broken rule.

headline: Texas lobby reports with $1,000+ in gifts named a recipient 1 time in 4 in 2005-11; since 2019, 3.7%
number: 61 of 228 reports in 2005-11 vs 9 of 243 since 2019; the drop hit in 2012, and the same 15 filers went from 22 of 63 to 1 of 47
watch_out: If the itemization threshold jumped in 2012, it's a rule change, not lobbyists hiding names; that hasn't been checked.

headline: 1 in 4 new IRS political-group notices, Dec 2022-Dec 2025, came from businesses, including 141 look-alike companies
number: 2,596 of 10,464 new notices tagged business or charity (24.8%), vs 6.8% in 2019-Nov 2022 and 4.6% since Jan 2026; 8 of the look-alikes, in 7 states, filed within 31 minutes on July 8, 2025
watch_out: The business tag is a keyword rule (hand checks about 95% right), the batch rule isn't saved in analyze.py, and custodian names shouldn't be printed.

headline: 34 of Trump's 45 second-term judges (76%) got no Democratic votes; Biden's 2023-24 judges: 25% got no Republican votes
number: 34 of 45, including all 7 appeals judges, got zero Democratic or independent votes; Biden 32 of 130 (25%); without Collins, Murkowski and Graham, Biden's figure would be 58%
watch_out: Most of the gap is three Republican senators (Collins, Murkowski, Graham), and partisan confirmations are widely covered.

headline: The Senate held 659 recorded votes in 2025, second only to 1976; 356 were on nominations, a record since 1989
number: 659 Senate roll calls (1976: 700); after the Sept 2025 en bloc rule change, nomination votes fell from 37.3 a month to 12.6; 41.5% of 119th Senate votes had zero crossover vs 13.5% in the 118th
watch_out: Nominations are only tagged from 1989, so "record" can't reach further back, and the vote counts were covered in real time.

headline: Fetterman was the only Democrat voting with Republicans on all 12 Senate Iran war-powers votes; two failed by one vote
number: S.J.Res.163 failed 49-50 on 2026-05-13 with Ricketts absent; S.J.Res.172 failed 47-48 on 2026-06-16 with Sanders, Bennet and Booker absent
watch_out: The member-by-member table ends 2026-06-24, so two later Iran votes, one a 49-50 failure, are unseen.

headline: Argentina sided with the US on 78% of UN votes in 2024-25, up 19 points, biggest rise of 178 countries
number: 59% to 78% in the Sept 2024-Sept 2025 session; the typical country fell 13 points; Argentina ended third most out of step, behind only Israel and the US and level with Russia
watch_out: The session straddles Biden and Trump, so part of the rise may be the US changing its own votes; that split isn't done.

headline: Just 12% of House bills passed by roll call this Congress got an amendment roll call; the 1995-2024 median: 61%
number: 14 of 118 in the first 538 days (12.7% with data to 2026-08-08); same point 1995-2024: 39.2% to 74.1%, median 60.8%; the defense bills still drew 17 and 19 amendment votes
watch_out: No amendment roll call doesn't mean no amendments: voice votes and en bloc packages don't show in this data.

headline: 16 of 38 Supreme Court cases from the 5th Circuit in 2021-24 were federal-government appeals; in 2015-20, 1 of 26
number: 16 of 38 (17 counting the consumer finance bureau, CFPB); the other 11 regional circuits stayed at about 12% in both periods; Supreme Court cases per 1,000 5th Circuit appeals rose from 0.57 to 1.50
watch_out: The table this lead is filed under adds nothing; every count comes from the Supreme Court Database and the FJC appeals file.

headline: Jackson Area credit union (Mississippi) holds $148.2M in deposits on $71.4M in assets: a $77M hole
number: Deposits are 2.08x assets, the only one of 4,250 credit unions over 2x (median 0.86x); a $91.7M loss in Q1 2026 leaves net worth about -$77M (-107.9%)
watch_out: Only one quarter (Q1 2026) is loaded, and the account codes behind the $91.7M loss are labeled by matching the data, not NCUA's dictionary.

headline: Since 2020 the bank regulator (FDIC) put 11 of 107 minority-owned banks under cleanup orders: about 2.7x similar banks
number: 2020-26: 11 of 107 (10.3%) got a new bank-level consent order vs 86 of 3,167 peers (2.7%); matched on size and region you'd expect about 4
watch_out: Minority status is today's value and the order texts are unread; money-laundering orders on remittance-heavy banks could carry the whole gap.

headline: Boxlight insiders filed 30 of 76 stock-sale reports late; 38 of 2,740 companies ran 10%+ late; median zero
number: 38 of 2,740 companies with 30+ sale reports had 10%+ filed 11-365 days late (22 under the strict rule); 90th percentile 2.9%
watch_out: A late sale report is a paperwork failure, not proof of insider trading; co-owners filing the same trade twice can fake lateness (55 such mirrors were dropped).

headline: Since 2024, 31 per 1,000 money-manager stock reports ran a year-plus late, vs 9.5 before; Malaysia's pension fund back-filed 68
number: 31 of every 1,000 original 13F holdings reports (Jan 2024-May 2026) filed 1+ year late vs 9.5 per 1,000 (mid-2013 to Sep 2022); 105 managers back-filed 8+ reports
watch_out: Filings from Oct 2022 to Dec 2023 aren't loaded, so 2024 is when the wave shows up in the data, not proof it started then.

headline: At least 36 US-sanctioned banks still hold numbers on the tax agency's (IRS) foreign-bank list, including Russia's central depository
number: 36 OFAC-blocked institutions with a live FATCA registration (31 Russian, 3 Belarusian, 1 Armenian, 1 London); 5 match on the GIIN that OFAC's own record prints
watch_out: Only 5 match on an ID; the rest are name plus country. A blocked bank on the list is two Treasury arms disagreeing, not proof money moved.

headline: 355 fund holdings reports still count in thousands, not dollars: about $2.6 trillion missing, a third from T. Rowe Price
number: 355 of 8,631 original Q1 2026 13F reports in thousands (the rule has said dollars since Jan 2023); x1,000 that's about $2.6T; T. Rowe's own cover page totals $864,926,710
watch_out: 13F_SUBMISSION is an exact copy of the Mar-May 2026 window inside 13F_HOLDINGS; union the two and you double-count.

headline: 18 small public companies filed annual reports past the legal extension three years running; 4 still list on major exchanges
number: 18 past the 15-day extension FY2023-FY2025; 4 still list a Nasdaq/NYSE ticker: Laser Photonics, Global Interactive Technologies, BIO-key, EON Resources
watch_out: FY2025 lateness comes from audit-report dates, not actual 10-K filing dates; about half of the 439 FY2025 misses dated their audits inside the extension.

headline: Louisiana re-inspected only 90 of 182 hazardous-waste manufacturing plants in five years, last of 28 states; median 91.8%
number: 90 of 182 (49.5%) got another full on-site inspection in the five years to July 2026; next lowest Illinois 62.7%, Texas 66.5%
watch_out: An approved alternative compliance-monitoring plan would make this legal; not checked. Louisiana's small-generator inspections more than doubled over the same years.

headline: 40 of 102 working major cement plants drew a serious Clean Air Act violation in 2020-25, top of 63 industries
number: 39% of operating major cement plants got a new high-priority violation vs a 9.8% median industry; 3.7x other major plants in the same states
watch_out: Cement kilns run continuous monitors, so more breaches get caught; and the plant list may be padded with grinding terminals or bagging plants (Quikrete Calera, Systech Paulding).

headline: Yuma, Arizona's water plant broke the acute chlorine-dioxide limit 21 months straight; none reached federal records until May 2022
number: 21 acute violations, one a month Jul 2020-Mar 2022, readings 0.9-2.0 mg/L vs a 0.8 limit; 21 of 54 such violations nationally since 2015 (next-worst: 6)
watch_out: Code 13 is read as the acute chlorine-dioxide limit from the data, not EPA's code list; the public-notice violations closed 2022-06-02, so a notice probably went out late, not never.

headline: 17 landfills stopped filing federal climate reports with no legal way out; at least five hold operating air permits
number: 17 landfills on EPA's own "stopped reporting, unknown reason" list; median last report 85,741 t CO2e, 16 of 17 over 25,000 t; 11 flagged 5+ years
watch_out: Reporting year 2024 isn't loaded, and the Sept-2025 repeal proposal and rule changes aren't checked; an unprocessed exit notice would make it paperwork lag.

headline: Oregon logged zero state water-permit inspections in the federal file for 22 months; its warning letters kept arriving
number: 0 Oregon state inspections after 2024-09-30 through July 2026, after 161 in 2023 and 169 in Jan-Sep 2024; its letters kept coming (110 in 2025, 74 in 2026)
watch_out: The warehouse can't tell stopped inspections from a broken state data feed; one call to Oregon DEQ decides it.

headline: 433 wastewater permits broke discharge limits in most quarters for six years with no formal enforcement; Missouri 97, Ohio 68
number: 433 individual permits over limits in 8+ of 12 quarters in both 2020-23 and 2023-26, none with a formal action; Missouri 97 and Ohio 68, about half of each state's chronic violators vs 18% elsewhere
watch_out: State orders that never reach EPA's system look exactly like no enforcement; the data can't yet tell them apart.

headline: Cheniere's Sabine Pass gas-export terminal went from 0.18 to 6.26 million tonnes of greenhouse gas, 2015-23: the registry's biggest rise
number: +6.08 Mt CO2e, rank 1 of 6,021 facilities that reported both years (next: +2.90); seven LNG facility IDs went 0.38 to 16.48 Mt while all direct emissions fell 3,058 to 2,578 Mt
watch_out: It's a new-plant story: rank 1 needs the window to start before exports began (from 2017 it's rank 4), and emissions likely just track LNG shipped.

headline: Tesla's Fremont plant drew 356 Bay Area air violation notices since 2019, second of 86 plants; no district enforcement order
number: 356 notices written on 133 days since 2019; other heavily cited Bay Area plants got a median 28 formal actions per 100 notices; Tesla and Phillips 66 Rodeo (213 notices) got none
watch_out: The district may act outside the federal file (a 2024 abatement petition was reported); its last recorded action is a $1,000 order in 2014, and EPA's own $275,000 paint-shop penalty came in 2022.

headline: 438 place names still say "Negro"; in 2020-23, 641 "Squaw" names changed vs at least 41 "Negro" or n-word ones
number: 438 official federal names in the English sense (426 current, 12 historical); 105 list the n-word as an older name in the same file
watch_out: Citation dates stop on 2023-03-17, so renamings after that can't be counted by year; 50 Spanish "negro" (black) names were removed by hand.

headline: The 4th Circuit appeals court published 375 decisions in fiscal 2025, up 25% from 2019; the median circuit fell 17%
number: 375 published decisions FY2025 vs 299 FY2019 (+25%); published share 8.8% to 13.7%; 363 of the 375 were argued
watch_out: The FJC code meanings (published, argued) are read from the data; confirm them in the FJC codebook. The older +74% figure starts from a 2020 COVID low.

headline: Detained immigrants' release petitions (habeas): 33 in Oct 2024, about 8,820 in Mar 2026, 24% of new federal civil cases
number: About 8,820 new detention habeas cases in Mar 2026, 24% of 36,088 new federal civil cases; of 16,849 closed Oct 2025-Mar 2026, detainees won 7,340 and the government 831
watch_out: Winner and "closed without a ruling" codes are decoded from the data, not the codebook; half the closures have no winner coded, mostly dismissals.

headline: Since 2020 only 19 of 295 argued Supreme Court cases came from state courts, the lowest share since 1946
number: 6.4% since the 2020 term vs 14.1% (146 of 1,034) in 2005-19; state courts' share of petitions held at about 27%
watch_out: The petition side leans on CourtListener's appeal-from field, which misses many state appeals courts; the finding may already be known in legal scholarship.

headline: One building at 410 Great Rd, Littleton, Massachusetts holds 49 separate federal gun-maker licensees, 16% of the state's
number: 49 of Massachusetts' 303 maker licenses (type 07) at one address; only two US buildings hold 10+ separate maker licensees, both in Massachusetts
watch_out: Renting suites to licensees is legal: this is a feature, not proof of wrongdoing, and the building key is a hand-cleaned address.

headline: Vermont logged 77 private-sale gun background checks in 2022: 0.17 per 100 dealer checks, last of 10 states requiring them
number: 0.17 private-sale checks per 100 dealer checks; median of the 10 law states 2.2; median of states with no law 0.10
watch_out: The dealer picks the "private sale" code, so this may show how Vermont sales get logged, not that sellers skip the check; the table stops at Sep 2023.

headline: 10 foreign groups hold 40% of US "social welfare" nonprofit assets, $133.4B; Mastercard Foundation and Novo Holdings lead
number: $133.4B of $335.2B in 501(c)(4) assets; Mastercard Foundation (Toronto) $50.3B, Novo Holdings (Denmark) $36.2B; without those two, 20%
watch_out: The share runs 39-41% depending on double counting (Novo Nordisk Fonden may own Novo Holdings) and on foreign groups at US addresses; the status is legal and may be tax-neutral.

headline: Customs refunds beat collections in May and June 2026; $113.5B left via the customs agency by Aug 7
number: June 2026: $49.18B refunded vs $23.63B collected (net -$25.56B); Jun 29 alone $35.49B; the FY2023-25 pace was $40M a day
watch_out: The likely cause (court-ordered refunds of the emergency IEEPA tariffs) comes from a Federal Register notice, not the money tables; the warehouse copies stop Jun 30 (monthly) and Aug 7 (daily).

headline: EU registrars renewed 11 of 13 sanctioned firms' global company IDs after listing; 9 still current, including four Iran-linked banks
number: 11 of 13 renewed after the EU listing, like ordinary clients at the same offices (72-98%); London's registrar renewed 0 of its 4 UK-listed clients
watch_out: Renewal may be lawful: EU rules allow licensed fees for upkeep of frozen assets and prepaid multi-year plans are common; 6 of the 8 renewed links come via OpenSanctions, not an ID the EU printed.

headline: Homeland Security committed $50.97B in contracts Oct 2025-Jun 2026, 4.1x its usual; Fisher Sand & Gravel got $13.35B
number: $50.97B vs a $12.42B median for the same nine months of FY2019-2025; border-barrier construction at CBP is $27.0B of it
watch_out: The agency table's "32 cents paid per dollar committed" leaves a $192B gap five times the contract jump; reconcile the $281.3B DHS figure before using it.

headline: Federal injury filings (OSHA) cover 18-24% of Vermont's private hospital jobs, vs 88-94% typically; University of Vermont Medical Center absent
number: OSHA 300A summaries for 2023-2025 cover 18-24% of Vermont's 13,453 private general-hospital jobs; median state 88-94%; Hawaii 33-48%, New Mexico 24-38%
watch_out: Vermont, New Mexico and Hawaii run their own state OSHA plans; if those never adopted the electronic filing rule (1904.41), it's a rule gap, not missing filings.

headline: The tax agency revoked 108 nonprofits for not filing, yet its own e-file index holds a return from those years
number: 108 auto-revoked 2019-2026 with a return received for one of the three missed years; 59 still unreinstated and off the exempt list; 27 quietly put back without a recorded reinstatement
watch_out: A late or wrong-form return received before the revocation date may not legally stop auto-revocation; get the IRS rule in writing. The claimed 6x time trend is an e-file-mandate artifact; drop it.

headline: 296.5 million Indians face severe hunger, by the UN food agency's own math, though it leaves India's line blank
number: 296.5M in 2022-24 = Southern Asia (363.4M) minus FAO's "Southern Asia (excluding India)" row (66.9M); 35% of FAO's 836.5M world total, up from 205.6M in 2014-16
watch_out: FAO never prints 296.5M; it's a subtraction of two FAO regional rows, so confirm how FAO builds regional totals (its SOFI technical annex) before print

headline: Holly Springs, Mississippi's city utility never billed 42.6% of the power it bought in 2024, worst of 425 city utilities
number: Bought 240,422 MWh (megawatt-hours) in 2024, billed 137,809; billed fell 224,000 (2022) → 178,000 (2023) → 138,000 (2024) while purchases held at 232,000-251,000; the median city utility loses 3.4%
watch_out: Only 2024 is in the warehouse (the 2019-23 trend came from EIA files pulled outside), and every check is the city's own filing, so a bad EIA filing is not ruled out

headline: Ohio utilities spent $3.22 per customer on saving electricity in 2024; Michigan, next door, spent $81.98
number: $3.22 per customer ($8.38 with utility-run demand response), 48th of 51 states; national median $31.09 ($39.50 with demand response); first-year savings 0.063% of Ohio's sales vs 1.692% in Michigan
watch_out: One year only (2024), and "no row" for Duke Energy Ohio and Dayton P&L may not mean no program: demand response sold through the PJM grid market never shows up here

headline: FirstEnergy's seven utilities still send people to read 2.26 million meters, about 27% of all hand-read US meters
number: 2,260,839 hand-read meters in 2024: about 27% of the US total (30% if EIA's estimated small-utility meters are left out) on 3.8% of all meters; its Ohio, Maryland and West Virginia utilities hand-read 57-83%, every other investor-owned utility there under 5%
watch_out: 2024 only and self-reported; if regulator-approved smart-meter rollouts are underway, this catches FirstEnergy mid-swap: "late", not "refused"

headline: Ten coal plants made 30% of all monitored power-plant sulfur dioxide in 2025; Labadie, Missouri, alone made 5.3%
number: 217,766 of 715,725 tons of SO2 (sulfur dioxide) from the 1,179 smokestack-monitored plants that emitted any in 2025; Labadie 38,232 tons; 7 of the 10 have no retirement or fuel-switch year on file with EIA
watch_out: Legal, not a violations story: the plants sit under loose limits in a federal allowance market, and EIA's retirement field misses coal-to-gas conversions

headline: Phoenix-area Salt River Project has 56.7 rooftop-solar homes per 1,000; Arizona Public Service has 145.4, Tucson Electric 124.3
number: 56.7 net-metered home solar systems per 1,000 homes in 2024; in 2014-19 SRP added 9.7 per 1,000 while Arizona Public Service added 61.7 and Tucson Electric 47.4
watch_out: The 2014 and 2019 numbers come from EIA files downloaded outside the warehouse, and nationally SRP is not low: 20th of 102 big utilities, 3.4x the median

headline: 89.7% of Evergy's Kansas City homes in Missouri are on time-of-day rates; across the state line, 1.6%
number: Evergy Metro homes on time-varying rates, 2019 to 2024: Missouri 0.1% → 89.7% (245,547 homes), Kansas 0.1% → 1.6% (3,904); all four Missouri investor-owned utilities went from near zero to 76-99%
watch_out: Enrollment counts are each utility's own filing, and utilities choose whether to count homes moved by default (SCE 57.8% vs SDG&E 0.6% under one regulator)

headline: Alabama Power reports 1.6 watts of rooftop solar per home, last of 173 big utilities; sister Georgia Power: 30.1
number: 2.1 MW of home solar across 1.33M homes (2024); median of the 173 utilities with 100K+ homes about 120 W; Southern Co. sisters Georgia Power 30.1 W and Mississippi Power 31.5 W; Alabama Power has no net-metering row
watch_out: These are the utilities' own reports and EIA allows best estimates; if an outside count is far higher, the story becomes "Alabama Power under-reports", not "Alabama homes don't go solar"

headline: One Google ad account named only "US House of Representatives" carries 58% of members' official-office Google ad money in 2026
number: $811,700 of $1,391,800 (58%), weeks of Jan 4-Aug 2, 2026, up from about 6% in 2019-21; since 2022 its district ads aimed at seats held by 88 different members, none named on the account
watch_out: The total's 3.3x jump over 2024 is mostly the market (House campaigns' own Google spend rose 1.8x in the same weeks); the pooled account is the finding, not the growth

headline: Homeland Security spent $5.29 million on Google ads that Google filed as political, the only federal agency in 2018-2026
number: $5,285,100, Mar 2025-Feb 2026 ($4,294,000 in 2025, $991,100 in 2026): #3 account of calendar 2025 and #13 of the 2026 cycle through Aug 2, out of 4,892
watch_out: Why Google filed the ads as political is untested, and DHS's 2025 ad campaign was already news; the new part is Google's political filing and the week-by-week curve

headline: 13,265 people who arrived by 2021 were detained in Jan-May 2026, 3.8 times 2024, the low year
number: Immigration-court records: 13,265 detentions Jan-May 2026 vs 3,490 Jan-May 2024; ICE's stay records show 3,083 → 11,567 for Jan-Feb; for people here 10+ years, 5,760 vs 3,076 in Jan-May 2019 (1.9x)
watch_out: 2024 was the low point: against 2019 the rise for 10+ year residents is about 1.9x, and entry dates are filled less often now, so every count is a floor

headline: At 45 big companies, contractors' H-1B work-visa filings listed wages a median 20.6% below the company's own, same job
number: Median 20.6% lower at 45 client companies (39 more than 1% lower), same job code and state, FY2019; at the same skill level the gap is 6.6%; new-hire filings only, 14.5%
watch_out: One year (FY2019), name-only client matching, and most of the gap is the skill level the contractor writes down, so the claim is "filed lower", not "paid less for the same work"

headline: 16,919 immigration detention stays began with over a day in an ICE hold room, Oct 2025-Feb 2026, up from 212
number: 16,919 stays (14.8% of stays that started in a field-office hold room) vs 212 (0.8%) in the same months two years earlier; Baltimore: 3,041 of 3,168 stints over a day, median 87 hours
watch_out: Facility type is one snapshot label and it's wrong both ways: Mesa's "Hold" site works as removal-flight staging (a fifth of the count), and Chicago's Broadview is typed Staging, leaving out 1,968

headline: Company formations in England and Wales fell 73% on 18 Nov 2025, the day identity checks became compulsory
number: 847 new companies on Tue 18 Nov vs 3,156 the Tuesday before; the five weeks from 17 Nov ran 29% below the six weeks before (11,158 vs 15,790 a week), at least 16,000 fewer; 10,338 of 64,456 company numbers (16%) match no company
watch_out: The dip didn't last (January 2026 ran 4-7% above January 2025), and Companies House may already have published it

headline: 28% of new Irish companies in 1992 sat at addresses holding 1,000+ companies; by 2001, just 1.2%
number: 4,136 of 14,669 in 1992 (28.2%); 23 addresses took 33,458 companies in the 1990s and 1,870 since; 68% of those 1990s companies were struck off in 1999-2000 vs 32% elsewhere; 41 Central Chambers, Dame Court, Dublin 2 holds 8,826
watch_out: History piece, and the register keeps each company's last address, not its first; consecutive company numbers at one address (45% vs about 5% by chance) are the evidence of formation there

headline: Offshore formations doubled in Apr-Jun 2005, just before Europe's savings tax; Panama firm Mossack Fonseca: 2,331 to 4,701
number: Apr-Jun 2004 → 2005: Mossack Fonseca 2,331 → 4,701, Bahamas registry 1,656 → 3,108, Nevis registry 684 → 1,353; middlemen with Swiss, Luxembourg or Monaco addresses carry 69% of Mossack Fonseca's jump; Asia-facing providers rose 12-13%
watch_out: History piece, probably covered in outline by 2016 Panama Papers reporting (not checked); the middleman on file is the firm's client of record, not proven to have ordered each formation

headline: 339 of Atlantic City's 1,473 public housing units sit empty without an approved reason: 23%, 5.9 times similar authorities
number: 339 "regular" vacancies of 1,473 units (23.0%) in HUD's July 2025 file: highest of 91 non-"Moving to Work" authorities with 1,000-4,999 units, 5.9x their 3.9% median; almost half at Stanley Holmes Village, 50% occupied
watch_out: A $450K Choice Neighborhoods grant (FY2021) means units held empty for redevelopment aren't ruled out; setting Stanley Holmes aside, 12% of the rest are still regular vacancies (3.8x peers)

headline: Around Red River Parish, Louisiana: zero magnitude-2.5+ quakes 2010-2023, then 29 since January 2024, topped by a magnitude 4.9
number: 28-by-78 km box: 0 events of M2.5+ in 2010-2023 (none within 50 km either); 16 from Jan 2024 to Mar 4, 2026 (biggest M3.6); M4.9 on 2026-03-05; 12 more by May 3, including M4.1 and M4.4 on Mar 9
watch_out: Natural quakes aren't ruled out, and 11 of the 12 post-M4.9 events came after a station went in within a few km, so later counts mix aftershocks with better detection

headline: Union Pacific trains killed 156 trespassers a year in 2023-25, nearly double 2015-17's 79; other railroads, same counties: up 30%
number: UP-reported train-strike trespasser deaths: 79 a year (2015-17) → 156 (2023-25); UP's full count, including non-train deaths on its property, 97 → 200; other railroads in the same counties rose about 30%
watch_out: A third of UP's recent reports use a stand-in age of 40 (4% in 2015-17), so part of the jump may be a change in how UP files; there's no suicide field

headline: In Ecuador's Los Ríos province, 29 of 66 town-hall public-works tenders drew one bidder; about 7-8 was expected
number: 29 of 66 (44%) one-bidder works tenders in Jan-Jun 2026 records, highest of 24 provinces (coastal town halls elsewhere 15%, Guayas 21%); $13.4M of $28.8M, $6.3M of it one Quevedo contract
watch_out: RECORD_DATE is the release date, not the award date: about a third are late-2025 tenders and 2025 holds no tenders, so there's no year-over-year; one bidder is a screen, not proof

headline: The Justice Department's Epstein site said "access denied" for data sets 13-23 and "not found" for 24-40, March 11, 2026
number: A 19:26 probe, one address a second: 13-23 got DOJ's full-size 403 page (about 10.46 KB), 24-40 its 404; the switch came inside one second; the only other full-page 403 in 1.54M captures was data set 9, five weeks before its Jan 30 release
watch_out: Each of data sets 13-40 has exactly one capture, so "never live" rests on a single look, and reading 403 as "built but unpublished" isn't confirmed against DOJ's site software

headline: FEMA, the disaster agency, took a median 110 days to publish Jan-Jun 2025 disaster declarations, versus 41-48 days before
number: Median 110 days from declaration to FEMA's first Federal Register notice for Jan-Jun 2025 disasters vs 41-48 in 2023-24; California's January 2025 fires waited 223 days; FEMA printed declaration notices on 3 days in Jan 2025-Aug 2026, while SBA printed the same disasters in 1-3 weeks
watch_out: FEMA's batch "omnibus" notices carry no DR number in the docket, so a DR-number join misses them; check the notice text before calling anything a first notice

headline: 74-90 California doctor-shortage areas holding 2.7-3.5M people are up for removal with no replacement, about 3x the national rate
number: Builder: 123 of 214 active California shortage areas (57%) proposed for withdrawal, 4.62M people; after removing areas already re-designated under new IDs, 74-90 areas and 2.7-3.5M people remain.
watch_out: 4.62M counts people already re-designated under new IDs (1.06M of the 2.91M "still designated" sit on the same tracts); 85% of the July 2026 withdrawals are old IDs retired after re-designation.

headline: Male veterans' suicide rate rose about 10% in 2018-23 whether or not they used VA care; under-55s carry it
number: Men using VA health care: 48.5 to 53.4 per 100,000 (+10.1%), rising every year; veteran men outside VA care: 36.21 to 39.71 (+9.7%); non-veteran men flat, 29.3 to 29.0.
watch_out: No join, and it's VA's own published appendix; the age-adjusted rate puts 71% of its weight on under-55s, who carry the whole rise, and the widening gap comes from VA's modeled headcount while veteran male suicides fell.

headline: Claimed: DeRoyal's Tennessee sterilizer tied #1 for ethylene-oxide air releases; broken, a Virginia sterilizer reported 5.3 times more
number: Sterilization Services of Virginia (Henrico), an FDA-registered contract sterilizer, reported 8,995 lbs in 2024; DeRoyal's matched site (1135 Hwy 33 S) filed 1,205 lbs, #3 among contract sterilizers and down 8% since 2018.
watch_out: The "1,705 lbs at the site" adds two separate FDA sterilizer registrations, and the peer median swings from -45% to -11% depending on the match rules. Drop the DeRoyal story.

headline: Penn State's Hershey hospital got Medicare's extra "outlier" payment on 185 of 192 top-level joint procedures; nationally, 3.5%
number: Penn State Health's 5 hospitals: $12.35M in outlier add-ons vs $0.76M expected (16.3x, the top of an 8-16x range); Hershey and Lancaster carry 93% of it.
watch_out: Medicare's own published formula explains it (Hershey ranks #3 of 1,726 on charges x cost-to-charge ratio); "57% of big hospitals get $0" is wrong (a blank means 1-10 cases, real figure 84 of 1,212), and "half to 50 hospitals" skips 16,053 hidden cells.

headline: Medicare's new back-pain program roster names 3 doctors barred from federal health programs and 13 who opted out
number: 3 of 6,510 participants on the OIG exclusion list (all pain doctors), 13 on the Medicare opt-out list; other pain doctors are excluded at 0.16% vs 0.26% inside the model, 3 people vs 5.
watch_out: The "same-state" base rate covers all states and most of the ~4x gap is specialty mix; 11 of 13 opt-outs took effect after the model was proposed, so they may be a reaction to it, not a missed screen. The whole effect is 3 people.

headline: Only 37 suppliers billed Medicare's diabetes-prevention classes for 11+ patients in 2024: 1,267 patients, $347,437 in all
number: 37 suppliers, 1,267 patients, $347,437 (median supplier 22 patients) against 1,037 listed sites; at most about 3,800 patients even counting every hidden small supplier.
watch_out: Low use is already reported; "existed before 2024" used the NPI issue date (40 of the 228 joined in 2024-26), the California line counts 64 Kaiser sites that joined in 2026, and Maryland's share is two suppliers, one mostly online.

headline: Guttmacher puts Texas, a total-ban state, at 3,530 abortions a month in early 2026: up 26%, one December 2024 jump
number: Texas averaged 3,530 a month in Jan-Mar 2026 (range 3,017-4,147) vs 2,797 in Jan-Mar 2024 (+26%); flat since the Dec 2024 jump.
watch_out: The jump sits right on a method seam: ban-state months before Jan 2025 carry no low-high range, every month after does. Guttmacher also publishes this trend itself.

headline: Enbrel's two FDA-approved copies never went on sale; Medicare drug plans ran up $2.27B gross on brand Enbrel in 2022
number: $2,269.6M Part D gross drug cost for Enbrel in 2022 vs $0 for its copies (Erelzi 2016, Eticovo 2019, both listed discontinued).
watch_out: Circular: Enbrel was picked because its copies read 'Disc', and a copy never sold has $0 sales by construction; pooled across all 11 molecules, copies took 0.89%, not the 16.6% median.
