headline: Kindred's 42 long-term hospitals book $178M a year more expense than Medicare's cost line; the peer gap is accounting
number: A fast-growing $178M-a-year gap between booked expense and Medicare's cost figure; on Medicare's cost line the Kindred-vs-peer margin gap shrinks from 9.4 points to 0.8.
watch_out: Kindred's -6.7% vs +2.7% margin is on booked expense; on Medicare's cost line the gap is 0.8 points and the same-state test falls from 11 of 13 states to 7 of 13.

headline: In 2023, six California fiberglass shops put out about 40% of the state's reported cancer-list air pounds, mostly styrene
number: Styrene is about 55% of California's cancer-listed air pounds once sulfuric-acid mist (319,746 lbs) is counted, not 74.5%; the six shops about 40%, not half.
watch_out: The CAS join can't see group listings like sulfuric-acid mist (CAS '---'), which drops styrene to about 55%; and California is 7th of 44 states on styrene share, a pattern already found in deep-2 and g38.

headline: This Congress passed 63 regular laws in its first 539 days, second-fewest since 2013; only the last Congress passed fewer
number: 63 laws that aren't rule repeals, renamings or spending bills by day 539 of the 119th (builder said 67); the 113th-117th had 93-145 at the same point, the 118th 43.
watch_out: "Regular law" is a title-keyword cut, not a classifier (it misses CRA votes titled "Disapproving the rule"); the fall 2025 shutdown (68 days with no laws) is an untested dull explanation.

headline: 20 of 69 Georgia U.S. House races in 2010-18 had nobody running against the winner; nationally it was 4.8%
number: Georgia 20 of 69 (29%) with no runner-up; nation 4.8% (builder said 4.0%); median state 0.
watch_out: "Georgia leads, Alabama next" is false (Massachusetts ranks higher); more than half the gap is plain one-party districts, and Georgia's "barely moved" skips 0 of 32 in 1990-94.

headline: Federal Election Commission totals for House Republicans' campaign arm skip its Sept 2024 report: $40.72M of spending
number: The NRCC's (C00075820) 2024 line is $21.88M off its own cash math because its Sept 2024 monthly ($40.72M spent, $18.85M raised) is missing from FEC totals; its own filings balance to the cent.
watch_out: The NRCC story is dead: its own filings reconcile to the cent. The error is the FEC's roll-up, and API /totals matches the bulk file, so it can't serve as the outside check. One committee, no story until the FEC comments.

headline: Only 16 of 83 retirement-eligible Republican-appointed judges stepped back in Trump's second term; 50 had already stayed through his first
number: 16 of 83 (19.3%) took senior status in the first 517 days; 50 of the 83 (60%) had already passed on it under Trump 1, vs 20% of Trump 1's own pool.
watch_out: Within each group (fresh vs already-passed) Trump 2 is ordinary (z about 0.5); the "record low" is Trump 1's leftover stayers, and the yearly series has lower same-party years (12.2% in 2020).

headline: Sen. Richard Blumenthal filed all 69 of his stock-trade reports on paper, 2021-2026; the warehouse holds none of his trades
number: 69 of 69 periodic transaction reports on paper, Feb 2021 to Aug 2026; since 2024, 43 of the Senate's 44 paper filings are his.
watch_out: Legal and public: the scans sit on the Senate site, the habit goes back to 2012, and g12 plus deep-6 already found it; "since 2024, 43 of 44" is mostly other senators leaving or switching.

headline: 139 campaign funds for races run by 2016 still hold $7.98M; Robin Tallon's 1992 committee paid out $1.39M in 2023-24
number: $7.98M cash across 139 committees (median $366; 3 hold 59%; 32 terminated); Tallon for Congress paid out $1,391,737 in the 2024 cycle with $0 from individual donors.
watch_out: TTL_DISB is all money out, not spending: it includes Byrne's $300K payback to himself and likely investment purchases. This also repeats g28's Tallon lead.

headline: RA Capital filed as director at 21 companies in 2024, OrbiMed 16, Baker Bros 13; eight firms drive biotech's lead
number: Investment firms filed as director at 91 of 708 biotechs (12.9%) vs 24 of 372 software companies (6.5%) in 2024; without eight firms, biotech is below software in 2022, 2023 and 2024.
watch_out: Eight firms carry the whole biotech-vs-software gap, so the "sector" test is really a test of RA, OrbiMed and Baker Bros; a 4-year window cuts the gap to 1.4x and counting 10% owners to 1.25x.

headline: EPA sent Osage County, Oklahoma oil-field wells zero violation notices after April 2023, while still inspecting about 225 a year
number: Osage injection-well notices: 88 in 2022, 2 in 2023, 0 since April 2023; formal cases on the same wells held at 14-18 a year.
watch_out: The builder's headline is broken: the 54 Jan-Sep 2024 notices went to small drinking-water systems, not wells, and the Oct 2024 "stop" is those notices moving to another EPA system (SFDW went 12 to 172).

headline: A third of small, non-exempt US-listed foreign companies missed a new March 2026 insider-stock deadline by 13+ days
number: China/HK small issuers trail other small foreign issuers by 12 points, not 16, once blank-country firms are placed; vs non-Israel peers p = 0.08, vs Asian/US/Australian peers p = 0.53.
watch_out: DERA leaves the business-country field blank on ~40% of late-2025 rows, which misfiled 26 China/HK firms as "other"; what's left of the China gap depends on one peer country, Israel.

headline: Senegal's government foreign-debt payments due in 2026 equal 54% of its 2024 export earnings, top of 108 poorer countries
number: $4.44B scheduled for 2026 = 54.0% of 2024 exports; Bhutan 50.2%; median of 108 low- and middle-income countries 8.4%.
watch_out: One ~$1.06B bond payment due in 2026 is what puts Senegal ahead of Bhutan; on 2027 or the 2026-28 average it drops to #2. The World Bank publishes this ratio itself.

headline: Companies late on stock-option award reports in 2017-20 stayed late in 2021-24: roughly 13% vs 1.5% for peers
number: Builder: 20.3% of 2021-24 awards 30+ days late at the 23 repeat companies vs 1.5% at 1,248 peers; skeptic's rough cut without Security National is about 13% (not re-run). AgEagle: 85 of 117 awards 30+ days late.
watch_out: The #1 contributor, Security National, is a stock-dividend re-report artifact; AgEagle's 2021-24 lates sit on catch-up filing days; "option awards" also counts warrants, convertible preferred and RSUs.

headline: 189 old campaign funds paid out $8.57M in the 2024 cycle; 19% went to candidates, parties and PACs, not 2.1%
number: $8,569,194.71 out from 189 committees (median $1,794.61); the committee-to-committee file shows 19.4% to candidates, parties and PACs (23.5% with loan repayments), not the 2.1% seen in gifts to candidates alone.
watch_out: The 2.1% came from checking only gifts to candidates; the committee-to-committee file shows 19.4%. The exact-name filter also let sitting politicians' committees (Ted Cruz, Tom Kean Jr) into the list.

headline: 41 super PACs named for police, veterans and sick kids raised $181.5M; roughly 4% reached real political spending
number: Builder: at most $22.5M (12.5%) to politics, 2017-24; 73% of the itemized ad money paid a phone and caging vendor block, so real political spending is closer to 4%. That six-vendor block is paid only by sympathy-named committees, 24 of 24.
watch_out: The 66.5% peer is big-donor super PACs; small-dollar peers send only 6.5-8.7%. 46% of the dollars are j8's FEC twins, so it isn't a new lead, and the count is a floor (2 Piaro PACs, $18.75M, were dropped).

headline: 3 of 748 big credit unions lost 20%+ of net worth in a year: Civic, Greater Nevada, U.S. Eagle
number: Net worth -39.5% (Civic FCU, $3.19B), -30.3% (Greater Nevada CU, ratio 3.33%), -20.6% (U.S. Eagle FCU); they rank #2, #4 and #1 of 758 on loans 60+ days late.
watch_out: The late-loan rank isn't a second witness (same call report, same mechanism) and the ACCT_041B label is unconfirmed; Greater Nevada is profitable with low charge-offs yet lost $24.5M of net worth, unexplained.

headline: 19 water systems serving 4,347 people buy only from sellers that broke a chemical limit; their own records look clean
number: 19 systems and 4,347 people after cleanup (builder said 99 and 45,518); a buyer carries a chemical violation 8.4% of the time when its seller violated, 0.3% when the seller is clean.
watch_out: The flagship was misread: Saline Valley's arsenic violation sits where it buys Millstone's water, and Harrisburg plus nine towns drink its clean well water. The rule charges the seller by design.

headline: EPA's database shows Nebraska with 24 of 66 plants nationwide holding an old, serious air violation never acted on
number: 24 of 66 facilities (36%, 17-36% depending on the cutoff) with a high-priority violation from before July 2024, unresolved, no formal action ever; on Title V major sources alone, 5 of 40.
watch_out: ADM Columbus isn't in the 24 and only 4 of the 7 named ethanol plants are; 19 of the 24 aren't Title V sources, and a records gap is likely (Nebraska's formal actions in the database fell 89% at the 2014 system switch).

headline: Diamondback's Permian Basin frack jobs drew 1.6-2.3 times the fresh-groundwater share of other reporting drillers in 2025
number: Gap 1.6-2.3x in 2025 against operators that report water, 1.2x across all years; the builder's 40.5% vs 10.4% (about 4x) didn't hold, and "22% of wells" is really 9.3%.
watch_out: The 4x was basin mix (Diamondback's Midland Basin wells vs a peer group 71% in the Delaware Basin) plus a groundwater-only count; the biggest home-county peers file no water rows at all.

headline: The Pentagon's tech agency renewed Ivanti's often-hacked phone-management software each spring: $21.8M+ since 2023, on a fixed calendar
number: $21,771,170 on 6 DISA awards, May 2023 to Apr 2026 (skeptic: really 9 DISA awards; federal EPMM spending at least ~$43.8M); 7 exploited EPMM holes listed in that window.
watch_out: The "$8,043,000 four days after the listing" is the yearly license renewal for a June 1 start (DISA has ordered in Mar-May every year since 2017); "paid" should read "obligated".

headline: US coal power rose 85 terawatt-hours (13%) in 2025, about 1.8 times every other country's coal rise combined
number: +84.99 TWh (+13.03%); the 23 other risers among 89 countries with 2025 data added 36.26 TWh (2.3x), about 1.8x once Ember's Asia residual for missing countries is added.
watch_out: It is a rebound: 2023-24 lost 179 TWh when gas was cheap, and 2025 wins back 85 while staying 94 TWh below 2022. 105 countries, Indonesia included, have no 2025 data.

headline: Texas gas plants able to switch to oil rose from 4.9% to 6.0% of capacity after the 2021 freeze
number: ERCOT 3,508 MW of 63,770 MW gas winter capacity (5.5%; 6.0% on the generator flag), up from 4.9% before Uri; SPP fell 17.2% to 13.6%, MISO 18.5% to 17.8%.
watch_out: "Less than half of SPP and MISO" is north vs south: SPP's southern states sit at 4.7% (Oklahoma 1.0%) and MISO's at 6.7%; the switch flags are self-reported by operators.

headline: Four unnamed traders held 69.7% of sell positions in one mid-Atlantic power futures contract in early 2026, a record
number: Top-4 share of the short side, PJM Western Hub off-peak day-ahead futures on ICE: 69.7% in 2026 Q1 (peak week 71.8% on 2026-03-10) vs 47.4% in 2024 Q1, but only about 5 points over the 2014-15 highs.
watch_out: One exchange only: the same product on Nodal Exchange sits near its low (~32%), 2024 is the series' lowest point, and the CFTC never names the traders.

headline: FEMA couldn't confirm occupancy on 28.6% of downtown Lahaina's fire-aid registrations; adjusted, the gap to neighbors is 7.5-9 points
number: Tract 314.04: 3,261 registrations for 3,223 residents (1.01, 38 over the line); 71.4% verified vs 86.3% and 88.1% in the other two burn tracts.
watch_out: About 40% of the unverified said it wasn't their primary home; the rest rests on one field (VERIFIED_OCCUPANCY) whose reason codes can't be read, and unburned neighbor 315.03 verifies lower still.

headline: Four people barred from Medicare show up in the offshore leaks at matching US addresses, out of 1,611 name hits
number: 1,611 name-only matches to the federal health-care exclusion list, 4 left with street or ZIP agreeing; 3 tied to Cook Islands asset-protection trusts.
watch_out: Golden held no trust (his nodes are middleman, protector and "nominated person"); the leak-vs-others comparison measures ZIP completeness, not behavior; Bressi and Roix match only at ZIP level through SAM.

headline: Justice Department's Epstein file list for Data Set 10 shrank from 10,071 to 5,569 pages, March to late May 2026
number: Data Set 10: 10,071 to 5,569 pages (about 225,000 file links out of the listing) by Mar 8; Data Set 9: 10,675 to 770 for about 4 weeks; both back May 22-23.
watch_out: Both "joins" are one Wayback crawl read twice, and the pager is flaky (Data Set 9 showed no pager for 16 days, Data Set 10 read 102 on Feb 1); a missing tail fits a search index refilling in file-number order.

headline: Coal operators who hand off a mine leave 16.6% of safety fines unpaid, vs 13.0% for those who close it
number: Builder: 28.7% unpaid at mines with 3+ operators vs 3.7% at one-operator mines; fair comparison, without Blackjewel/Revelation and Brody: 16.6% vs 13.0%, about 3.6 points.
watch_out: A one-operator mine can't carry departed-operator debt, so the builder's peer couldn't fail; Blackjewel/Revelation (0100767) and Brody (0070543) carry the dollars, and it's Central Appalachia only.

headline: 13 tankers seen in U.S. waters one January 2024 week now sit on government sanctions lists, most renamed
number: Older tankers (IMO below 9400000): 10 of 218 on government lists (4.6%, not 6.0%); newer: 3 of 732; 3 of the builder's 16 aren't sanctioned.
watch_out: No world base rate (the U.S.-feed rate may sit below it), and "served U.S. refineries" is backwards: hits are highest among ships that never stopped (5 of 50) vs 3 of 134 that tied up at a U.S. berth.
